newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent slides on profit-taking after rally.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent slides on profit-taking after rally.

text.p: SIMEX Brent futures traded $1.06 lower on profit-taking from its earlier high of $23.50 a barrel for October after the United States fired missiles on military targets in southern Iraq, brokers said on Tuesday.
"Players realise that the market has gone up too high and are selling off now for profit taking," one broker said. Brokers said an oil major was the most active buyer earlier in the day.

October last traded at $22.44, up 45 cents from its previous settlement on London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE), with November last traded at $21.60 up 47 cents from the last IPE close. November had earlier traded at a high of $23.10.

The market followed up on active trading that began on Monday to record 655 lots on Tuesday for October. Total volumes for the October-December contracts were over 785 lots compared with over 1,400 lots on Monday after the United Nations decided to delay the implementation of the oil-for-food deal with Iraq.

Latest reports quoted a western defence official in the Middle East as saying U.S. navy warships in the Gulf and B-52 bombers fired 25 to 30 cruise missiles on military targets in southren Iraq. Washington said the attack was in retaliation for Iraqi military attacks against Kurds in the north.
